label: Горячий / Холодный
description: Горячий vs холодный: hot/cold contrasts across genders and everyday scenes.

missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Masculine accusative agreement. 'Горячий' matches the inanimate masculine 'чай', whose accusative looks like the nominative. The breakfast scene anchors the thermal sense of the adjective.
Strategic focus: Feminine nominative agreement. 'Холодная' takes the feminine ending to match 'вода'. The simple image fixes the cold sense in daily life.
Strategic focus: Neuter predicate agreement. 'Холодное' matches the neuter 'молоко' as a predicate describing its temperature. The kitchen remark makes the neuter form concrete.
Strategic focus: Plural nominative agreement. 'Горячие' takes the plural ending to match 'кастрюли'. The stove scene fixes the plural form in mind.

missions.phrase: Он любит горячий суп, а не холодный.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Direct masculine contrast. 'Горячий' and 'холодный' both match the masculine 'суп', set against each other by 'а не'. One sentence pairs hot against cold.
Strategic focus: Masculine predicate adjective. 'Горячий' follows the noun as a predicate describing 'чайник'. The warning roots the thermal form in daily life.
Strategic focus: Masculine instrumental in the predicate. After past-tense 'был', 'горячим' takes the instrumental ending to match 'суп'. This shows the быть-plus-instrumental pattern.
Strategic focus: Plural instrumental in the predicate. After 'были', 'холодными' takes the plural instrumental ending to match 'напитки'. The sentence extends the pattern into the plural.
Strategic focus: Comparative form. 'Горячее' is the comparative of 'горячий' and stays the same for any gender. The comparison uses 'чем' to set two drinks side by side.
Strategic focus: Comparative of the opposite adjective. 'Холоднее' is the comparative of 'холодный' and is invariable. The seasonal note roots the form in a familiar scene.
